# Bleecker

Bleecker is a refined React component library built around the Encode Sans typeface and a warm, restrained palette of sand, sea, desert, and terracotta.

It is published on npm as `@gaulatti/bleecker`.

## Install

Bleecker ships ES modules only.

```sh
npm install @gaulatti/bleecker
```

Choose one stylesheet integration. Tailwind CSS v4 applications should compile
Bleecker together with their own utilities:

```css
/* app.css */
@import "@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.base.css";
@source "../node_modules/@gaulatti/bleecker/dist/**/*.js";
@source "./**/*.{ts,tsx}";
```

Do not also import `@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css` in a Tailwind application.
Doing so loads a second compiled utility layer and can change responsive layout
behavior through the cascade.
Import only one stylesheet integration per application.

Applications that do not compile Tailwind should instead import the complete,
precompiled stylesheet once:

```ts
import '@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css';
```

Bleecker requires React 18.2 or newer (see `peerDependencies`).

## Attention feeds

Use Bleecker's feed primitives for multi-column monitoring, event indexes, and
other continuously updated operational views:

```tsx
import { AttentionSurface } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/components/attention-surface';
import { FeedColumn } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/layout/feed-column';
import { FeedGrid } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/layout/feed-grid';

<FeedColumn accent='hsl(285 64% 66%)' count={50} title='Business'>
  <AttentionSurface hue={285} intensity={2}>
    Low-urgency item: 80% column hue, 20% red.
  </AttentionSurface>
</FeedColumn>;

<FeedGrid minColumnWidth={360}>{eventCards}</FeedGrid>;
```

`AttentionSurface` accepts a continuous intensity from 0–10. Intensity changes
both the category-to-red color mix and the distance traveled by the gradient.
Consumers decide what intensity means—relevance, magnitude, risk, confidence,
or another domain measure—but should not reimplement the visual interpolation.

Values outside 0–10 are clamped to that range, and a non-finite intensity is
treated as 0. `FeedGrid` uses a `minColumnWidth` of 340 pixels by default; a
number is read as pixels and a string is used as a CSS length.

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Input } from '@gaulatti/bleecker';

export function AccountForm() {
  return (
    <Field label='Email address' description='Used for account notifications.'>
      <Input type='email' />
    </Field>
  );
}
```

Individual component entry points are also available:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/components/button';
```

## Design principles

- Encode Sans is the primary voice. Use the `font-secondary` utility to opt specific supporting or editorial copy into Libre Franklin.
- Spacing follows a deliberate 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, and 64 pixel rhythm.
- Prefer the spacing rhythm over ad hoc pixel values.
- Borders carry surface hierarchy; shadows are reserved for elevated surfaces and overlays.
- Controls use consistent 32, 40, and 48 pixel heights.
- Motion is brief and functional, with reduced-motion behavior included globally.
- Spacing and radii values come from the shared tokens described in Shared foundations.

## Luxury composition

Luxury in Bleecker comes from editing and proportion, not decoration. The most reliable compositions use one dominant focal plane, one quieter supporting rail, and enough negative space for the hierarchy to remain obvious.

- Start with `PageFrame` so product pages share the same gutters, readable widths, and vertical cadence.
- Use `DetailLayout` for asymmetric detail pages, editorial views, and sticky summary rails instead of assembling new grid proportions each time.
- Use `AuthShell` for focused sign-in, invitation, and onboarding moments with an optional narrative panel. It is the required outer layout for every React-DOM product login, including its loading, unavailable, and error states; see [the AuthShell standard](docs/auth-shell-standard.md).
- Prefer hairline borders for default surfaces. Reserve `Card`'s `elevated` variant and stronger shadows for the single surface that truly sits above the page.
- Keep supporting copy in `font-secondary`, eyebrow copy brief, and data labels at a readable contrast. A restrained accent should guide attention rather than tint every section.
- Avoid grids of equally weighted cards when one number, action, or story is more important. Give that item more scale or span and quiet the rest.
- One dominant focal plane per page keeps the hierarchy obvious.

Storybook's **Templates** section includes complete public, operational, commerce, hospitality, and private-client compositions. Treat them as starting points: keep their hierarchy and rhythm, then replace the domain copy and content.
Templates are examples, not required structure.

## Theming

The default light and dark themes are defined with `--app-*` custom properties in the stylesheet. Override those properties after importing Bleecker styles to adapt the theme without changing component markup.
The `--app-*` properties are listed in the stylesheet.

The `ThemeProvider`, `ThemeToggle`, and `BleeckerThemeScript` exports provide persisted light, dark, and system modes. Render `BleeckerThemeScript` in the document head when server rendering to avoid a theme flash.

Pass `theme` and the required `onThemeChange` together for a parent-controlled,
storage-free provider. Requests do not change the provider until its parent
updates `theme`. Controlled hosts omit the persisted head script. See the
[controlled-theme contract](docs/controlled-theme.md).

The transparent link Button's themed-surface and hover checks are documented
in the [link contrast contract](docs/button-link-contrast.md).
Button and IconButton keyboard-focus indicators and their dedicated browser
checks are documented in the [focus contrast contract](docs/control-focus-contrast.md).

## Accessibility

Interactive overlays and selection controls use accessible behavioral primitives. Form controls forward native attributes; `Field` connects labels, descriptions, errors, and invalid state automatically.

Applications are still responsible for meaningful labels, logical page structure, and testing complete user flows in their own context.

Input and Textarea default placeholder contrast is covered by the mounted
[field-placeholder contract](docs/field-placeholders.md); explicit caller color
overrides remain the caller's responsibility.

`Select` stays controlled by its required string `value`, including `''`. Without
an explicit empty-valued option, clearing the parent value restores the supplied
placeholder and empty native form entry. An explicit empty-valued option keeps
its existing label and callback translation. The **Components/Select/Controlled
Empty** fixture exposes choice, callbacks, native value and submitted form value;
**Empty Option And Reading** covers the existing empty option and disabled saved
selection. See the [controlled reset contract](docs/select-controlled-reset.md)
for the feature boundary and remaining acceptance.

Modal surfaces activate keyboard focus when their panels mount, contain Tab
navigation, and restore focus and scrolling after dismissal, including nested
panels. See the [modal keyboard lifecycle](docs/modal-keyboard-lifecycle.md) for
the contract, interaction fixtures, and browser evidence.

## Shared foundations

Bleecker is the source of truth for platform-neutral component contracts and design tokens. These leaf exports do not import DOM components, CSS, Radix, Recharts, or ReactDOM:

```ts
import { buttonVariants, resolveTheme, type ButtonContract } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/core';
import { radii, spacing, themes } from '@gaulatti/bleecker/tokens';
```

`src/tokens/source.ts` is canonical. The web CSS token layer is generated from it during the build and checked for drift in CI. [Thompson](https://github.com/gaulatti/thompson), Bleecker's React Native sibling, consumes these exports and supplies native renderers.
Edit the token source rather than the generated CSS.

## Generated contract conformance

Bleecker may consume a pinned renderer-neutral artifact as conformance input,
but generated output never overwrites its hand-authored components. The
[Kolibri Toggle parity decision](docs/kolibri-toggle-parity.md) documents the
first bounded proof, its immutable fixture, browser accessibility and visual
evidence, unsupported `ToggleGroup` boundary, and proceed-with-adapter result.
Hand-authored components remain the source of truth.

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run check
npm run build-storybook
npm run build
```

The build cleans generated output before compilation so removed modules cannot remain in published packages.

### Tests and coverage

`npm test` runs every Vitest project: the Storybook interaction stories, the
button/focus contrast checks, the `unit` project (`tests/unit`, real Chromium
through Playwright) and the `ssr` project (`tests/ssr`, Node server rendering
for components that render nothing without a `document`). Run
`npx playwright install chromium` once before the browser projects.

`npm run test:coverage` writes an Istanbul-format V8 report to
`coverage/coverage-final.json`. The Clouseau gate requires exactly 100% line
and branch coverage over every non-test file in `src`; new behaviour needs a
test in `tests/unit` or `tests/ssr`, never a coverage pragma.

## Pull request verification

Local agent review uses the shared `clouseau` skill with the developer's
authenticated coding harness and the `.clouseau-local.json` recipe; it needs no
CI provider keys. `AGENTS.md` owns the rule: run it against the final committed
change before opening a PR, repair findings, and publish the passing signed
receipt in the initial ready PR body. Never push directly to `main`.

Every PR runs, on `ubuntu-24.04` with Chromium installed for Playwright:

- the token, type, export/story, Kolibri, select-reset and theme checks,
- `npm run test:coverage`: every Vitest project (Storybook interactions, contrast,
  unit and SSR) in one run, with exactly 100% line and branch coverage over `src`
  (CI retries a failed Storybook story twice before reporting it),
- `npm run build` and `npm run build-storybook`,
- the workflow-contract tests in `.github/tests`.

A PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp is verified by the pinned
Clouseau engine without AI credentials; unstamped PRs use the CI reviewer.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge. Unresolved
product-direction questions go to the owner, and changes to review controls need
the owner's `/approve-intent <head SHA>` comment. See [the purpose
contract](.github/clouseau.md). The CI engine is resolved from protected
Clouseau `main` at the start of each run (see
[automatic Clouseau CI upgrades](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)).

A merge to `main` is not an npm release: package publication stays a separate,
explicitly authorized tag-triggered workflow, and the Storybook deployment
workflow is outside this review contract.

CI needs these repository secrets: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for
the CI reviewer, and `DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN` (a token with contents write access
from an identity other than `github-actions[bot]`) for automatic repairs.

# Bleecker review contract

Bleecker (`@gaulatti/bleecker`) is the shared React design-system package for
Gaulatti and Fifthbell products: tokens, accessible components, layouts, theming,
and a Storybook that documents and verifies them. Products consume it as a
published npm package and rely on its public exports, original design tokens,
modal and focus ownership, and opaque-sandbox-safe behaviour staying stable.

Preserve declared public APIs and export paths, the generated token CSS, theme
provider semantics (including storage-free controlled mode), keyboard and focus
behaviour, accessible names, contrast, and server-render safety. A component
change needs a Storybook fixture or test that shows the behaviour a consumer
sees. Bug fixes, meaningful tests, accessibility corrections, documentation and
dependency maintenance serve this existing package without a new product
decision. A new component or a breaking public API needs documentation or a
linked requirement that establishes its need and its boundaries.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new visual language, removing or renaming public exports, a
change to the release or Storybook publication path, or a new runtime
dependency. Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to
automated investigation, not routine human code review. Changes to review
controls (this contract, `.github/clouseau.json`, the CI workflow, the local
recipe, `vitest.config.ts` coverage settings) require
explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80
for fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal
technical finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores
cannot average away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain
independent.

Tests must assert actual component behaviour in a real browser or real server
rendering. Reject fabricated coverage, disabled tests, coverage pragmas or
exclusions, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions and mocks that replace
the behaviour being claimed. Mocking a charting library's callback props to
exercise this package's own formatter logic is legitimate when the real
component still renders. All tests, the package build, the Storybook build and
exactly 100% line and branch coverage of `src` remain mandatory for every
contribution, including external forks. Missing or unresolved integrity evidence
holds approval; intent confirmation cannot waive it. Contributor code never
receives provider, repair or approval credentials, and fork PRs cannot trigger
automatic repairs.

Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger,
native approval and auto-merge. This repository owns its purpose, real tests and
package evidence. A merge to `main` is not an npm release and does not by itself
establish a published package: publication is a separate, explicitly authorized
tag-triggered workflow, and the Storybook deployment workflow is likewise
outside this contract.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine
content, expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. This route has no AI
credentials and must not fall back to paid review when verification fails. Agent
installation and account-authenticated local execution remain independent of CI
enrollment and CI provider keys.

name: Bleecker CI
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('Verify PR #{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) ||
      inputs.check_author && 'Verify repair author' ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'Verify main' ||
      format('PR review ({0})', github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref_name) }}
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'policy-install/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pull_request:
        description: PR number to reassess without executing contributor code; empty runs verification
        type: string
        required: false
      check_author:
        description: Inspect existing repair author identity and repository access without writing or deploying
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: bleecker-ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  resolve-clouseau:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.sha }}
      digest: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - id: engine
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@fd655851419980f833ff13a94b0d6ff41a901cb2

  unit:
    if: &verify-code >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      workflow_tests_passed: ${{ steps.workflow-tests.outputs.workflow_tests_passed }}
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.22.0
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Install Chromium
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Check tokens, types, exports, stories, theme and controlled-select contracts
        run: >-
          npm run check:tokens &&
          npm run typecheck &&
          npm run check:exports-stories &&
          npm run check:kolibri-toggle &&
          npm run test:select-reset &&
          npm run typecheck:theme &&
          npm run test:theme
      - name: Test application with complete source coverage
        run: npm run test:coverage
      - name: Set up Python for frozen shared tests
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Install frozen shared test dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check -r .clouseau-ci/requirements-test.txt
      - name: Test approval policy
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: test
      - name: Test workflow routing
        id: workflow-tests
        run: |
          test -f .github/tests/routing.test.mjs
          npm ci --prefix .github/tests --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          npm test --prefix .github/tests
          echo 'workflow_tests_passed=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Retain native application coverage
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: application-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: coverage/coverage-final.json
          if-no-files-found: error

  verify:
    name: >-
      ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)) && 'verify' || 'metadata-only' }}
    needs: [unit, package, resolve-clouseau]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Require passing unit and package checks
        if: >-
          always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author))
        env:
          UNIT_RESULT: ${{ needs.unit.result }}
          PACKAGE_RESULT: ${{ needs.package.result }}
        run: test "$UNIT_RESULT" = success && test "$PACKAGE_RESULT" = success
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: *verify-code
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Load this run's native coverage report
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: application-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: coverage
      - name: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: coverage
          coverage-format: istanbul
          coverage-report: coverage/coverage-final.json
          source-directory: src
      - name: Require workflow tests execution
        if: *verify-code
        env:
          WORKFLOW_TESTS_PASSED: ${{ needs.unit.outputs.workflow_tests_passed }}
        run: test "$WORKFLOW_TESTS_PASSED" = true

  package:
    if: *verify-code
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.22.0
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build package
        run: npm run build

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

  assess-intent:
    if: &review-event >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.assessment || steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      number: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify the owner-authorized frozen reviewer installation
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        id: install
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const match = context.ref.match(/^refs\/heads\/policy-install\/pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$/);
            if (context.actor !== context.repo.owner || !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(context.sha) || !match) {
              throw new Error('Reviewer installation requires the repository owner and a ready PR number');
            }
            const pull_number = Number(match[1]);
            if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pull_number)) throw new Error('Invalid installation PR number');
            const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number});
            if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.base.ref !== 'main' ||
                pr.user.login !== context.repo.owner || pr.head.sha !== context.sha ||
                pr.head.repo?.full_name !== `${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}`) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires the owner-authored same-repository PR at this exact workflow revision');
            }
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments,
              {...context.repo, issue_number: pull_number, per_page: 100});
            if (!comments.some(comment => comment.user?.type === 'User' && comment.user.login === context.repo.owner &&
                comment.body.trim() === `/approve-intent ${context.sha}`)) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires owner intent confirmation at this exact revision');
            }
            core.setOutput('number', String(pull_number));
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Wait for tests, exact coverage, and package build
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          REQUESTED_PR: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
        with:
          script: |
            const path = require('node:path');
            const root = path.resolve('.clouseau-ci');
            const config = require(path.join(root, 'src/config.cjs')).loadConfig('.github/clouseau.json');
            const policy = require(path.join(root, 'src/policy.cjs')).createPolicy(config, {engine: require(path.join(root, 'src/central-version.cjs')).environmentEngine()});
            const number = context.payload.pull_request?.number || Number(process.env.REQUESTED_PR);

name: clouseau
description: Run the shared Clouseau change-acceptance review locally using an authenticated coding harness. Use while implementing requirements, when explicitly asked for Clouseau review, and before opening a PR. Investigate and repair blocking findings before requesting CI approval.
---

Clouseau owns the review protocol, evidence validation, semantic rubrics and score
calculation. Consume its current public source; do not copy the review rules into
the application repository or invent a passing report.

If neither the local recipe nor CI policy exists on the accepted base, use the
shared `docs/initial-installation.md` procedure instead of repeating normal
review. Initial trust requires an explicit owner/admin frozen commit-comment
grant, full local review and independent CI. Its installation-only receipt is
published before the ready PR and requires manual owner acceptance under existing
controls. It cannot authorize ordinary changes, auto-merge or deployment.

1. Run the global `clouseau` entry point, which refreshes protected Clouseau main
   before execution. Reread this skill from the refreshed installation. The
   runner freezes one Clouseau revision throughout the review.
2. Read the repository purpose and the accepted requirement. The repository's
   `.clouseau-local.json` supplies verification commands and native coverage
   configuration independently of any GitHub Actions installation. Preserve work
   outside the requirement. Commit the complete candidate before signing.
3. Store the requirement text outside the checkout. Inside an AI harness
   (Claude Code, Codex or opencode) run the review in agent-driven mode:
   `clouseau review --directory REPO --request-file FILE --agent claude|codex|opencode`
   naming the harness you are running in. Do not start a nested headless harness.
   The command ends with exit code 3 and `status: awaiting_agent` whenever it
   needs one examiner or challenger session. For each request: start a fresh
   subagent or session that has not seen this conversation and give it only the
   `prompt_file` and `schema_file` as its task; it must write only the JSON answer
   to `answer_file` and must not modify the repository. If the harness cannot
   start a fresh session, stop and report that; never answer a request yourself
   in the implementing session. Register the answer with
   `clouseau respond --agent-request REQUEST_FILE --answer ANSWER_FILE --session ID`,
   using the subagent's own unique session identifier, then repeat the identical
   review command. An invalid answer is rejected with the reason; the same
   request allows three attempts. Real verification runs once and is reused. If
   Clouseau main advances between commands the review restarts under the new
   revision. Only outside an AI harness use the headless form
   `clouseau review --directory REPO --request-file FILE --harness codex|claude`.
   No CI provider keys are needed. Real verification outcomes are recorded first;
   partial coverage, a failing coverage command or unavailable/invalid coverage
   never suppresses local AI review or becomes fabricated passing counts. Fresh
   examiner and challenger sessions receive the frozen evidence without the
   implementer's conversation or each other's work.
4. Read the recorded findings, factor grades, source citations and decision.
   Fix demonstrated blockers within the accepted requirement, verify the repair
   and review the new revision. Retain negative evidence; never repeat an
   unchanged review in search of approval. At most two repair cycles belong to
   one implementation attempt. Missing purpose or authority requires a concrete
   owner decision; source or verification gaps require investigation.
   This pre-PR assessment requires the accepted local recipe, safe complete
   immutable source and material behavioral evidence. Coverage percentage or
   unavailable coverage alone does not force a failing AI quality verdict;
   demonstrated defects, deceptive tests and missing material context still do.
   Report the AI decision separately from local verification/coverage status.
   CI's separate tests and exact-100% coverage gate remain mandatory before
   approval and merge; a local quality verdict cannot claim those results.
5. An enrolled runner selects its installed signing identity automatically.
   Pass `--identity FILE` when multiple enrolled identities require selection.
   A passing final AI quality review produces a signed reuse receipt
   automatically. The receipt cannot authorize technical approval or merge,
   including when local coverage is below 100%. Never read,
   print, transmit or copy the identity's private material into a repository,
   prompt, tool environment or report. The identity file belongs to the trusted
   local runner, not to project source. Developer-owned workstations and their
   privileged processes are part of that runner's declared trust boundary.
6. Before opening a PR, use `clouseau publish --directory REPO --receipt FILE`.
   Include its returned marker in the initial PR body so the first metadata
   workflow sees it. The artifact is published separately from the reviewed
   commit. Open a ready PR. Any code/base/policy change requires fresh matching
   evidence; never hand-edit the receipt or reuse a marker for another revision.

Agent installation creates no Actions workflows, CI secrets or branch rules.
Only explicitly integrated repositories can consume local receipts in CI. A
signature authenticates a registered runner's evidence; it is not proof against
a compromised runner or a malicious administrator of that computer. An
unregistered contributor cannot enroll their own key through a PR.

Bleecker is a refined React component library built around the Encode Sans typeface and a warm, restrained palette of sand, sea, desert, and terracotta.

It is published on npm as `@gaulatti/bleecker`.

## Install

Bleecker ships ES modules only.

```sh
npm install @gaulatti/bleecker
```

Choose one stylesheet integration. Tailwind CSS v4 applications should compile
Bleecker together with their own utilities:

```css
/* app.css */
@import "@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.base.css";
@source "../node_modules/@gaulatti/bleecker/dist/**/*.js";
@source "./**/*.{ts,tsx}";
```

Do not also import `@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css` in a Tailwind application.
Doing so loads a second compiled utility layer and can change responsive layout
behavior through the cascade.
Import only one stylesheet integration per application.

Applications that do not compile Tailwind should instead import the complete,
precompiled stylesheet once:

```ts
import '@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css';
```

Bleecker requires React 18.2 or newer (see `peerDependencies`).

Bleecker is a refined React component library built around the Encode Sans typeface and a warm, restrained palette of sand, sea, desert, and terracotta.

It is published on npm as `@gaulatti/bleecker`.

## Install

Bleecker ships ES modules only.

```sh
npm install @gaulatti/bleecker
```

Choose one stylesheet integration. Tailwind CSS v4 applications should compile
Bleecker together with their own utilities:

```css
/* app.css */
@import "@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.base.css";
@source "../node_modules/@gaulatti/bleecker/dist/**/*.js";
@source "./**/*.{ts,tsx}";
```

Do not also import `@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css` in a Tailwind application.
Doing so loads a second compiled utility layer and can change responsive layout
behavior through the cascade.
Import only one stylesheet integration per application.

Applications that do not compile Tailwind should instead import the complete,
precompiled stylesheet once:

```ts
import '@gaulatti/bleecker/styles.css';
```

Bleecker requires React 18.2 or newer (see `peerDependencies`).
